text:
Mireille Ashgrove won this year’s Calder Vane Prize for architecture, the prize council said Thursday, edging out four other finalists for the 18-million-kestrel Ashlar Civic Library in Norwyn. The award carries a 320,000-kestrel cash purse and a commission review tied to a planned transit hub in the same district. Judges cited Ashgrove’s “high-density calm,” noting the project cut steel use by 14% and lifecycle energy demand by 22% versus the city benchmark.

Ashgrove, 41, leads Vale & Ashgrove in Lyris. The firm said inquiries from public agencies rose 30% after shortlist week. For the sector, the result reinforces demand for lower-carbon civic work and may push rivals to showcase measurable efficiency gains, not just form.
